question: In France, law enforcement officers break up crowds of protesters by using excessive amounts of tear gas. Tear gas is considered a non-lethal weapon because it is only slightly toxic. It is used by the police to disperse protesters.

Nevertheless, some people who menstruate have reported adverse reactions after being exposed to tear gas: menstrual disruption, pain, uterine cramping, contractions, miscarriages, unexplained or heavy menstrual bleeding, or the worsening of symptoms of endometriosis. These first-hand reports are backed up by a US study from 20231. This is not the first time we have heard such warnings.

Nevertheless, France is still not funding research into the effects of tear gas on women’s gynaecological health, including on pregnancy, breastfeeding or endometriosis, or on the health of people taking hormones. On the contrary, the country continues to use these weapons, including on students under the age of 18. Given that France uses tear gas more than any other country in Europe, will the Commission: 1.
order France to stop using tear gas, as a precautionary measure?
fund a European study into the effects of tear gas on the health of women, girls and people taking hormones?
guarantee people’s right to demonstrate without having to put their health on the line, as provided for in the Charter of Fundamental Rights?
